summary: The broker keeps the socket open and sends an error text frame naming an expired token: the feed stops publishing and does not connect again until the trader logs in (audit RB-10).

notes: The web marks the session fatal on this frame (_on_ws_message, _is_fatal_auth_error, _mark_fatal_error) and, when the socket closes, retries with the token in its database a bounded number of times and stops when that token is unchanged (_run_websocket). The desktop's token changes only with a new login, so HdfcSecuritiesFeed::parse answers the frame with AuthFailed (investright::text_events, shared with HDFC Sky) and the manager stops until the next login.
web.json has no frame for the error push: text frames publish nothing on the web.

After the error frame the case subscribes SBIN: the desktop answers it with the session-ended message (the bridge reports the feed's AuthFailed status) and sends nothing upstream. The web keeps its socket until the broker closes it and would still queue the subscribe (subscribe_scrips). The step is what pins RB-10: with the error frame ignored the subscribe succeeds and reaches the broker.
After the error frame the feed closes the socket itself ({"close": null}) and opens no other connection; a feed that ignored the frame would keep the socket open.

deviations.reason: HDFC Securities sends lastTradeTime in epoch seconds (the web's own test pairs lastTradeTime 1700000000 with packetTimestamp 1700000000000); the web sends it unconverted as ltt, a docs key that is epoch milliseconds (docs/prompt/websockets-format.md). The desktop converts it to ms (investright::trade_time_ms). Lead decision: ltt in seconds -> ms, web defect (wrong unit).

A cash equity's packet carries no OI (proto3 writes oi 0); the web sends that 0 as oi and open_interest instead of leaving them out (web openalgo#2376). The desktop counts OI on the derivative segments only. Lead decision: web zeros for values the stream did not send are left out, web defect.
